text.p: SYDNEY, May 21 - LME copper prices flew to a one-year peak on Tuesday, bouncing strongly from negative territory and setting the scene for a test of the key $2,500 per tonne mark, traders and analysts said. Investment funds, commission houses, banks and the trade covering shorts were all said to have contributed to a burst of buying that swept the market higher in the last minutes of the kerb.
In Chicago, the Commodities Research Bureau index fell 2.14 points to 251.00.

On the LME, three month copper touched a peak of $2,495, the strongest since May 20, 1996 when prices hit $2,525. Last official business was at $2,493, up $19 on the day, but in after-hours trading copper was indicated at $2,504/09 at 1655 GMT.
Most of the other metals followed copper down and back up, but aluminium and nickel remained mired in negative territory.

Aluminium was shaken when stocks rose by 2,050 tonnes, the first increase since early April and prices broke out of a $1,650-$1,680 range they had held for the past 10 days. The market, however, seemed reluctant to sink too deep and stabilised after hitting $1,637 support. The market ended the kerb with pared losses of $6 at $1,647.
Stocks also affected nickel, which sunk to a low of $7,650 after inventories rose by 1,260 tonnes. This market also managed a bounce, finishing the day $165 weaker at $7,690.
The other markets mimicked copper, exploring the downside but rebounding back into positive territory.
Zinc edged down to $1,332, but ended the kerb $11 firmer at $1,353, while tin took a look at $5,715 but finished with a $45 gain at $5,790.
Lead added $3 to $623 and alloy finished at $1,500/10.

New York precious metals ended firmer Tuesday, relieved that the U.S. Federal Reserve will keep interest rates unchanged as it continued to fret about possible European central bank gold sales. After the New York market was closed, German Chancellor Helmut Kohl stepped into the fray over the country's plan to reevaluate Bundesbank gold by insisting there was no question of selling any of the central bank's reserves. COMEX June gold settled $1.50 firmer at $343.40 an ounce, traded $344.20 to $342.60. Bullion was quoted late afternoon at $342.70/$343.20.

CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed sharply lower on crop weather and on a collapse in soybeans, traders said. "Wheat and corn followed beans, and prospects of rain coming into the Western Plains also drove wheat down," said Joel Karlin, vice president of commodities for Chicago-based brokerage house Everen Securities. CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed four to 14-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with July down 14-1/4 at $3.80-1/2.

IPE Brent crude ended weak on Tuesday, dragged down by the expiring NYMEX June contract and a reversal of midafternoon gains on U.S. products which refocussed attention on refining margins. July Brent closed 14 cents lower at $20.02 a barrel, 18 cents above the low but well below the session high of $20.36 a barrel.
